2. The facts, in short, necessary for the disposal of the appeal are that the respondent No.1 borrowed Taka 50,000,00 from respondent No.3 Standard Chartered Bank and mortgaged the property mentioned in schedule A of the plaint of Title Suit No. 35 of 1996 renumbered as Title Suit No. 261 of 1999 and the borrower defaulted in repaying the loan and so the aforesaid bank filed the above suit for realising the money and obtained a decree of Taka 1,45,61,562 and the decree holder bank instituted Execution Case No. 23 of 1999 for recovery of the money by putting the aforesaid property in public auction and the auction took place on 2-9-2002 and the appellant auction purchased the property. The judgment debtor alleging irregularities in holding auction filed Miscellaneous Case No.10 of 2004 praying to set aside auction sale dated 2-9-2002. The decree holder bank contested the case filing written objection. The present appellant i.e. auction purchaser, also contested the aforesaid miscellaneous case by filing written objection denying the allegations of the judgment debtor. The learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat by judgment and order dated 17-2-2005 dismissed the miscellaneous case with costs. The judgment debtors being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order of the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat filed First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 66 of 2005. The High Court Division by order dated 29-3-2005 admitted the appeal for hearing and stayed further proceedings of Artha Rin Adalat Execution Case No.80 of 2005 for one month from date. 

 6. Mr Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed appeared for the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and reiterated his submissions made earlier and submits that the appeal was filed within 30 days from the date of the order of Artha Rin Adalat i.e. within the statutory period of limitation. According to Mr Ahmed, to examine legality of the impugned order it is necessary to probe into the question as to what is the "time requisite for obtaining certified copy" in this case and replying to the same he submits that since petition for certified copy was filed on 17-2-2005 and the copy was delivered on 7-3-2005; time requisite for obtaining the certified copy is 18 (eighteen) days and so the appeal could be filed within 6-4-2005 i.e. 30 days from 17-2-2005 + 18 days, the time required for obtaining the certified copy. 

 9. He further submits that even if a restricted meaning is given to the phraseology "time requisite for obtaining certified copy" and only 5 (five) days time is allowed for the same i.e. 3-3-2005 to 7-3-2005 (the date on which the certified copy was obtained), in that case also the appeal would be maintainable because the appeal was taken up for action i.e.“কার্যার্থে গ্রহণ’ (for hearing under Order XLI, rule 11 of the Code) on 29-3-2005 and 50% of the deposit was made before such date and this, according to Mr Ahmed, satisfied the requirement of section 41 (2) of the Ain. 

 "1. 17-2-2005 Misc. Case dismissed by the Ex. Court. 

 2(a). 28-2-2005: The case was transferred from 4th Court to 3rd Court of Artha Rin Adalat. 

 13. Thereafter Mr Khan submits that from the aforesaid chronology of events it appears that application for certified copy of the order of the Artha Rin Adalat was filed on 17-2-2005, the very date of passing the order by the Artha Rin Adalat without wastage of a single day and in view of transfer of the case from one Court to another on 28- 2-2005 the respondent filed another application for the certified copy as requisites for preparation of the certified copy were not assessed on the first application filed by the appellant on 17-2-2005. 

 1. 	Dismissal order of MisceIlaneous Case No. 	10 of 2004 passed by 	17-2-2005 

 21. The persistent case of the respondent, on the other hand, is that the memorandum of appeal being filed on 19-3-2005, within clear 30 days of the order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, the said memorandum must be deemed to have been filed in time. 

 22. The further case of the respondent is that under sub-section (2) of section 41 the appeal shall not be accepted for action (কার্যার্থে গৃহীত হইবে না।) if the memorandum of appeal is not enclosed with proof of deposit of 50% of the decretal amount. In the instant case, the High Court Division passed order on 23-3-2005 directing the respondents to make the deposit. The respondents accordingly deposited the same on 27-3-2005 and, as such, the High Court Division took up the matter for action (কার্যার্থে গৃহীত ) on 29-3-2005 and thus passed the impugned order admitting the appeal and, as such, there is nothing wrong in the impugned order of the High Court Division. 

 25. In the instant case there is no denial that memorandum of appeal being filed on 19-3-2005 it was filed prima facie within time being filed within 30 days of the date of the order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat but filing of the appeal under sub-section (1) being dependent upon fulfilment of the requisite of sub-section (2) as to deposit of decretal amount, we are of the opinion that the contention of the appellant that the appeal was not filed in accordance with law cannot be brushed aside. 

 26. The persistent case of the respondents is that though they applied for certified copy on 17-2- 2005 but the requisites being not assessed on the said application till 3-3-2005 another application was filed for the certified copy upon which the certified copy was delivered on 7-3-2005 and so the period of limitation started from 3-3-2005 the date of filing of the 2nd application for the certified copy, more so the record of the case being transferred from the 4th Court to the 3rd Court of the Artha Rin Adalat on 28-2-2005. 

 28. We have already found that the respondent applied for certified copy on 17-2-2005 but on the plea of there being no assessment of the requisites till 3-3-2005 a 2nd application for certified copy was filed on 3-3-2005. As to the fate of the application filed on 17-2-2005 there is no satisfactory reply. But from the particulars furnished by the respondents it appears that on 30-3-2005 it was rejected. The petition was therefore alive at least till 3-3-2005. What prompted the respondents then to file a second application for certified copy on 3-3-2005 ? The delay in making assessment, even  if true, in our opinion; does not entitle a party to file a 2nd application in order of enable him to take advantage of starting fresh period of calculation to meet bar of limitation. Transfer of the case from one Court to another, in the instant case at the instance of the respondent, cannot also be a ground for filling a 2nd application for certified copy on the basis of which fresh period of limitation could be counted. 

 31. But from the facts and circumstances revealed in the case we do not find that the respondents could make out a case to entitle claiming limitation' from the date of filing of the second application for certified copy. 

 36. On perusal of the aforesaid provision we are of the view that though in section 7 there was clear prohibition for acceptance of any appeal, in case of failure to make deposit as required under sub-sections (2) and (3) of section 41 of the Ain 2003 it has not improved the situation in favour of a party intending to prefer an appeal. putting the obligation to enclose proof of deposit of 50% of the decretal amount with the memorandum of appeal under sub-section (2) inasmuch as filing or memorandum of appeal itself has been made dependent on (উপ-ধারা (২)-এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে) and subject to fulfilment of sub-section (2). 

 37. In this connection the decision in the case of Abdus Sattar and others vs IFIC Bank Ltd reported ill 52 DLR 4 may he referred to. In considering section '7 of the Ain of 1990 it has been held that the deposit was made on 5-4-1999 which was long after submission of the memorandum of appeal. The deposit being not in accordance with law could not be construed as proper and legal deposit. The same case reached the Appellate Division and has been reported in 52 DLR (AD) 122 approving the decision of the High Court Division holding, "At the time of tendering the memorandum of appeal before the High Court Division the appellant did not deposit half of the decretal amount in the trial Court. Nowhere in section 7 it is provided that such deposit beyond the period of 30 days from the date of decree is compliance with the requirement of section 7 for the purpose of entertainment of a memorandum of appeal. Even on the event of granting time by the High Court Division for depositing, the same as contended by the learned Advocate of the petitioner, the deposit in the instant case not having been made within the statutory time cannot be construed to be a valid deposit for entertainment of a memorandum of appeal." 

 We are of the view that in the present case due to nonfulfilment of the requirement of sub-section (2) of section 41 of the Ain no valid appeal was pending before the High Court Division. 

 41. We have already quoted section 41. The section appears in Chapter VII (৭ম পরিচ্ছেদ-আপীল ও রিভিশন) containing sections 40 to 44. The aforesaid chapter deals with the provisions of appeal and revision and Chapter VIII deals with miscellaneous provisions as to disposal of cases and the time for disposal of cases and the said Chapter 8 contains sections 45 to 59. Section 48 quoted above prescribes the mode for calculating the period of days. This provision is never meant to indicate the mode of calculating the period of limitation for filing appeal which has been included in a separate chapter i.e. Chapter 7 of the Ain. 

 42. On consideration of the aforesaid provision we hold clearly that this provision in section 48 of the Ain is limited only to count the time for disposal of cases having no connection whatsoever with the period prescribed for filing appeal, nay of making deposit as required under section 41 of the Ain. The position shall be more clear if we read sections 45 to 46, prescribing various period as to filing/disposal of case in the aforesaid separate chapter i.e. Chapter VII. In view of what has been stated above. we are of the view that, acceptance of the argument of the respondents that section 48 is applicable in case of tiling the appeal shall lead to a dangerous effect telling upon the legal jurisprudence of the country and such a view is therefore unwarranted.
